**Sub-item 1b — "The answer should state that a HashMap is mutable" (1 point)**

Award the point whenever the answer conveys, in any way, that a HashMap (or the HashMap-style map it recommends passing) can be modified after construction. The word "mutable" is not required: any functional description of modifiability suffices, such as "HashMap supports put/remove/clear" or "entries can be added after construction." Demonstration counts as well as assertion — a code example that constructs a `new HashMap<>()` and calls `put`/`remove` on it, or a behavioral contrast such as "singletonMap throws UnsupportedOperationException on put whereas a HashMap accepts it," each earns the point. Generic phrasing is acceptable so long as it is tied to the map type actually being recommended or used, e.g. "you must pass a mutable map such as the one created with `new HashMap<>()`" or "regular maps are mutable, unlike singletonMap." Mutability stated purely by contrast also counts, since the contrast entails it: "singletonMap is immutable, unlike a HashMap" or "singletonMap, in contrast to HashMap, cannot be modified" is enough on its own.

Deduct 1 point only if nothing anywhere in the answer indicates that a HashMap (or the HashMap-style map being used) can be modified — i.e., HashMap is never described as modifiable, never contrasted with the immutable singletonMap, and no code or behavioral description shows it being changed.
